dimension_assessments.summary: Eight accepted requirements state their primary behavior and negative boundary.

The window identifies classification, corroboration, patch lineage, scoped source-control operation, shared runtime identity, blocked approval identity, navigation, and hygienic debug capture capabilities.
Several nouns and key fields are named, but concrete schemas, producer/consumer payloads, conversion rules, and output guarantees are missing.
Canonical contract boundaries are explicit for weak integration, corroboration, identity, approval scope, navigation, and debug capture.
Graph patching states one transition, but transition atomicity and recovery are absent; blocked-episode and identity lifecycles are not defined.
Several canonical authorities are declared, but the decision authority for corroboration, effective identity, approvals, and policy enforcement is incomplete.
Each PlanUnit supplies owner_doc, implementation surfaces, and owner hints, including an explicit Source Control versus Orchestrator boundary.
Documents and actor classes are named, but concrete runtime producers, consumers, data paths, and responsibility handoffs are not.
Every reviewed PlanUnit carries explicit GUI relevance and rationale; graph lineage and debug capture are marked user-visible or inspection-related.
Negative constraints exist, but failure detection, degraded modes, retry/rollback, stale input, and recovery semantics are absent across the operational contracts.
Secrets and PII are recognized, but enforceable classification, redaction, access, retention, deletion, and incident handling are unspecified; navigation and approval authorization are also absent.
Runtime identity is said to span actors, but propagation, consistency, versioning, and reconciliation rules are missing.
Operational ownership is partly named, but SLOs, telemetry, enforcement, on-call/recovery behavior, and retention operations are not defined.
No volume, latency, lineage-depth, storage-growth, concurrency, backpressure, or capture-size constraints are supplied.
Request-centric HITL identity is superseded and serialized/generation artifacts are required, but versioning and migration policies are absent.
Prose acceptance criteria and plan validators exist, but executable runtime and GUI behavioral oracles do not.
Consequential discretion remains in classification, voting, persistence, identity propagation, approval lifecycle, navigation translation, security enforcement, operations, scaling, and migration.

Key terms such as first-class, high-impact, 2-of-3, compact, generation, shared identity, optional attempt, identity-native, allowlisted, and planned up front lack operational definitions in this window.
